served: video-EEG monitoring of a typical event
results: 1. interictal EEG: runs of generalized polyspikes and spike-wave discharges at 2-3 Hz lasting 3-4 s, predominating bifrontally and occasionally shifting laterally

2. video-EEG monitoring of a typical event: ictal body turning preceded by head version; although the clinical onset looked focal, the EEG showed generalized beta fast activity for 0.5 s followed by a generalized 2.5-3 Hz spike-wave discharge with maximum bifrontal amplitude
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Juvenile Absence Epilepsy, an idiopathic (genetic) generalized epilepsy syndrome.
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy (if the body turning represents axial myoclonia)
2. Epilepsy with Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures Alone (if the interictal 2-3 Hz discharges are subclinical and not true absence seizures)
3. Frontal Lobe Epilepsy (given the strong clinical focal features, though the generalized EEG makes this unlikely)
dx: Juvenile Absence Epilepsy, an idiopathic (genetic) generalized epilepsy syndrome.
